messages:
anita: Heads up - shortseq p95 jumped ~2.4x on canary after yesterday's merged changes (fused-attn refactor + batcher heuristics). Seeing it in prod canaries and CI perf tests. Anyone else seeing this?

mike: saw the CI perf failure too — decode_p95_shortseq went from ~12ms -> ~30ms on A100 in perf-matrix/shortseq. Failing job: https://ci.redwood/rel/7890 :grimacing:

ci-bot: [CI] perf/regression detected: job=perf-matrix/shortseq metric=decode_p95_shortseq change=+150% baseline=12.3ms now=30.8ms run=perf-matrix/7890

sasha: grabbed a distributed trace from canary. Early-stage stack shows an unexpected memcpy inside the fused-attn path during KV warmup. Flamegraph attached: https://perf.redwood/fg/abc123 (shortseq span highlighted)

anita: paste of the hot span (from trace):
```
# kernel: attn_fused_v2
# stack: attn_fused_v2 -> kv_prefetch -> memcpy -> decode_loop
cpu: 12ms, gpu: 18ms, memcpy: 9ms
```

julien: kernel-selector logs show a new decision: for shortseq we now wait up to 80ms for additional tokens before choosing the low-latency kernel. That wait looks like it's blocking the fast path in canary. Also noticed batcher emits `warmup_window_ms=80` from PR 4690 changes.

mike: kv-cache telemetry shows hit ratio dropping in first 10 tokens (was ~0.92, now ~0.6). Prefetch timing shifted so cache warmup is delayed -> more memcopies and fallback kernel usage. Possibly interaction between the new batcher warmup and fused-attn placement.

sasha: repro command I used (can reproduce locally):
```
python tools/repro.py --model redwood/open-attn-v1 --seq_len 16 --requests 200 --concurrency 8 --warmup 1
```
repro shows decode_p95 jump immediately after merge.

anita: which PRs touched those paths?

mike: two suspects: PR #4682 (fused-attn refactor, touches kernel glue and memcpy ordering) and PR #4690 (dynamic-batcher heuristics, introduces warmup_window_ms + wait logic). They landed in the same release batch.

julien: quick experiment results: revert 4690 (batcher heuristics) in canary -> p95 returns near baseline. Revert 4682 (fused-attn) but keep 4690 -> still slow. That points to batcher change as trigger, but fused-attn makes the symptom worse. Interaction bug.

sasha: proposed mitigation: temporary canary hold + revert PR 4690; then open smaller hotfix to adjust warmup threshold from 80ms -> 20ms and add a shortseq override to prefer low-latency kernel for seq<=32.

anita: plan: 1) hold canary rollout 2) revert 4690 in canary 3) run perf CI + repro script 4) if green, promote revert and ship hotfix 4691 with tuned warmup and extra tracing. Who owns? :raised_hand:

mike: I'll own the bisect + canary hold. Starting revert of 4690 on canary cluster now and running the repro + perf run. Will post logs here.

deploy-bot: Deploy canceled for canary cluster 'canary-eu' per request from @mike (action: revert PR 4690 in canary)

anita: thanks. Please capture the kernel_selector.choice and batch_wait_ms in tracing for the hotfix so we can confirm root cause in the postmortem. Add the flamegraph link and repro commands to the perf-run doc: https://docs.redwood/perf/shortseq-2026

julien: for the postmortem, let's also add a small unit test that asserts batcher doesn't block for >25ms for seq<=32 under synthetic load (to avoid regressions).

sasha: ack. I'll start a draft of the postmortem and add instrumentation PR that emits kernel_choice and kv_prefetch_latency tags.

anita: appreciate the quick response. Keep updates in this thread and we'll schedule a quick sync if the revert doesn't fully fix it. :thumbsup:
